description: How opstack workflows use the actual selected domain skills; this does not replace their full instructions.

workflows.adaptation: Use the existing discovery/router skills for their actual domains, then route to the relevant selected skill rather than substituting a generic recipe. The complete routing index covers all 146.

Use find-skills for capability discovery, databricks-data-discovery for Databricks data questions, openai-docs for its OpenAI scope, and hf-cli for Hugging Face resources. Keep codebase tracing grounded in the repository; these domain skills are not universal repository crawlers.
Use the applicable framework/modeling/design skill to shape the actual architecture. Do not apply a framework-specific prescription to an unrelated codebase.
Select the implementation skill that matches the codebase and follow its concrete patterns and supporting references. The workflow below manages delivery around that implementation guidance.
Use the matching reproduction, performance, language, or tracing skill to investigate the defect. Load additional domain skills from the routing index when the failing path requires them.

For code review, use review-agent’s introduced-defect criteria, complete-diff inspection, caller/test checks, precise findings, and read-only boundary. Add animation/UI/language review skills when those domains are in the diff. Review workers do not delegate further.

Combine Daryl’s standing state-machine review preference with the applicable domain’s persistence, concurrency, memory, or transaction rules. These sources inform the relevant domain; do not require LangGraph or Solana in a different project.

Use these actual design, worst-case content, mobile, gesture, motion, and library-selection skills as the UI review method. Read the matching SKILL.md and required references, then use the checklist below to coordinate and verify the result.

Use the domain skill’s actual validation method: evaluation/verifier evidence for agent work, evaluator construction for LangSmith, query validation for Databricks dashboards, and rendering checks for Manim. Keep checks proportionate and scoped to the domain.

Base design-preference capture on learn-taste: trace rules to the user, preserve their reason, never invent preferences, and respect its approval requirements. Use skill-creator when the requested reusable result is a skill. An explicitly approved exact rule does not need approval again; inferred or expanded rules do.

Use the selected installer/discovery/plugin guidance within its stated scope when extending or connecting the stack. Installing this already-bundled repository uses opstack’s local copier; it does not need to download the selected skills again or connect accounts.

Use the existing design/motion and capability-discovery routers in their domains, and the complete selected-skill index for other tasks. Recommend the actual relevant selected skill, with an opstack workflow only when coordination is needed.

Adapt the selected swarm skill’s task-table → dispatch → aggregate → targeted-retry structure to the client’s native subagent runtime. Keep one row per bounded work item and structured results; the main agent aggregates. Replace its QuickJS/PTC execution dependency with native client tools, while preserving the coordination pattern. Use review-agent for read-only review workers and eval-engineering when designing agent evaluation/verifier tasks. Daryl’s model-role and verification preferences govern orchestration.
